mancity_case.title: Manchester City FFP Case: Why They Got Banned & The 115 Charges

uefa_ban.allegation: Disguising owner equity funding as commercial sponsorship income from Abu Dhabi entities (e.g. Etihad, Etisalat) to bypass UEFA FFP deficit rules.
uefa_ban.cas_appeal_result: OVERTURNED by Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in July 2020.
uefa_ban.cas_reason: CAS ruled that UEFA's allegations were 'time-barred' under UEFA's 5-year statute of limitations rule. However, CAS upheld a €10M fine for obstructing and failing to cooperate with UEFA's investigation.

pl_charges_breakdown.description: Allegations that sponsorship money supposedly from UAE companies was actually paid directly by club owners (ADUG), artificially inflating revenue so the club could spend lavishly on transfers without reporting FFP losses.

Failure to disclose full payments to managers and players. Allegations include former manager Roberto Mancini receiving a secret second salary through Abu Dhabi club Al Jazira, and secret player image rights contracts.
Failing to comply with UEFA's Club Licensing and Financial Fair Play regulations submitted through the Premier League.

pl_charges_breakdown.category: Breaches of Premier League PSR Rules
pl_charges_breakdown.description: Breaching Premier League Profitability & Sustainability Rules (PSR) allowing maximum losses of £105M over a 3-year monitoring period.
Refusing to provide documents, delaying proceedings, and failing to cooperate in good faith with the Premier League's multi-year independent investigation.

potential_sanctions.detail: Massive deduction (e.g. 30 to 100+ points), potentially causing immediate relegation.
Expulsion from the Premier League and forced relegation to lower tiers of English football.
Stripping Premier League titles won during the investigated period (2012, 2014, 2018).
Multi-window transfer ban prohibiting new player signings and astronomical fines.
